week.worked: Monday night at Craven Cottage carried the whole week: João Pedro and Rogers made nineteen between them from two Chelsea picks, and Calafiori added nine from a defender who has since risen to £5.6m. Fifty points from a squad that had produced almost nothing by Sunday evening.
week.didnt: The expensive half. Haaland captained for two, B.Fernandes two, Mbeumo two, Shaw one — four picks costing forty million pounds and seven points between them before the armband doubled the smallest of them. Kerkez played ninety minutes at Newcastle and returned nothing.
week.next: He watched Palmer start the cup tie, set up the second goal and hear his manager say that to have a good team Chelsea need a great Cole — while owning the Chelsea forward and the Chelsea midfielder either side of him and not that one. Ownership has gone 11.7% to 15.2% in a week. The United block is the other half of it and it does not resolve tonight: Ipswich at Old Trafford on Sunday, a manager already being written about after a display described as having zero cohesion, and a deadline that falls two days before the window shuts. Holding is defensible. Holding a fourth week running because holding is what he did last week is not.

watchlist.name: Palmer
watchlist.note: Thirteen points on the opening night, the penalties, a start and an assist in the cup, and the manager naming him as the thing the team is built around. The only argument left against him is that Xabi has £15.5m in a striker who blanked.

watchlist.name: Gvardiol
watchlist.note: Nine points from City’s left-back at exactly Kerkez’s price, and Liverpool have spent their window on wingers rather than full-backs. This is an upgrade rather than a rescue, and City play at Palace before the weekend proper.

week.worked: The cheap end did all of it: Ajer eight at £4.5m and Schade three from a Brentford pair nobody else in the room owns, Szoboszlai eight, Calafiori nine, João Pedro eleven. Forty-nine points from a squad whose every worthwhile return came from £7.5m or less.
week.didnt: He put the armband on a United midfielder and the gloves on a United goalkeeper on the day United lost 2-0 at Hull: four from the captain, one from Lammens, two from Mbeumo. Ballard blanked, and eight points sat on the bench behind all of it.
week.next: The double-up is the decision, not the transfer. Captain and goalkeeper are both United, into a home game against an Ipswich side that has just beaten Sunderland and signed an Argentina World Cup winner, behind a manager whose first fixture is being written about as an inquest. His Brentford pair travel to Elland Road, where the opposing goalkeeper has two clean sheets from two and Leeds are still trying to sign a £30m winger. Nothing there needs buying tonight; the armband needs a reason.

watchlist.name: Ødegaard
watchlist.note: He owns an Arsenal defender and no Arsenal attacker. Eleven points at £6.6m is the cheapest way to fix that, and the room has now gone a full week without anybody doing it.

watchlist.name: Trafford
watchlist.note: Two clean sheets from two opening games at the same £5.0m he pays for a United goalkeeper who has one point and a defence that lost to two headers at Hull. The catch is that the fixture testing it on Sunday is his own Brentford pair.

week.worked: The best mid-price spine of the five: Ndiaye nine, Szoboszlai eight, Rogers eight, Calafiori nine, João Pedro eleven — forty-five of his fifty-eight from players priced between £5.5m and £7.5m, and no chip spent to get there. Second of the five, six off the top of it.
week.didnt: Twelve points on the bench, nine of them Gvardiol, who started at left-back for City while Hume and Shaw kept their places in the eleven. It is the largest bench score in the room and it is more than the gap between him and the man leading it.
week.next: Still an ordering problem rather than a shopping one, and the ordering got easier to argue this morning. City’s other defender spent last weekend playing central midfield and scored from a corner there, and his manager may use him that way again at Palace tonight — which is a defender who does not defend, and the exact thing already wrong with Hume, whom Sunderland pushed out to the right wing. The player on his own bench is the City defender who actually plays in the back line. Everton go to Bournemouth, who conceded eighteen set-piece goals last season and hired their first set-piece coach because of it.

watchlist.name: Ødegaard
watchlist.note: The only Arsenal asset he owns is a defender. At £6.6m the midfielder costs roughly what E.Le Fée does, and E.Le Fée produced no shots and no chances created.

watchlist.name: Tarkowski
watchlist.note: He already owns the Everton midfielder; this is the same fixture bought from the other end. Bournemouth’s set-piece record is the reason, and a £6.0m centre-back who attacks corners is the way to use it.

week.worked: Two Arsenal picks nobody else in the room has — Havertz and Mosquera — returned twelve, Tzolis added six, Verbruggen kept a clean sheet at £4.5m and João Pedro brought eleven. Five players costing £31.5m made thirty-five of his forty-eight.
week.didnt: Semenyo, his second most expensive outfielder at £8.5m, returned two from a starting City wide role. Maguire was in the middle of both set plays United conceded at Hull, and Greaves and Groß brought four between them. Forty-eight is last of the five.
week.next: Two of his four bench slots are still held by players who have never started a competitive game for their club — Palestra flagged at 75% again, Aït-Nouri behind the City left-back who has been playing. That is the cost he has been carrying since day one and it has not yet been charged to him. The one thing that would fix a bench slot cheaply is happening at Villa Park: a £4.5m Arsenal defender is expected to face his old club, and it is not one of his. His own Arsenal pair go to the same ground with the club chasing another striker.

watchlist.name: Palmer
watchlist.note: He has a Chelsea defender who has not played and no Chelsea midfielder. Thirteen points and the penalties at £9.5m is where the money he has in Semenyo belongs.

watchlist.name: Gvardiol
watchlist.note: The player keeping his own bench pick out of the City side, for exactly the same money. If a City defensive slot is worth holding, this is the one that starts.

week.worked: Sixty-four points, top of the five and second of eleven, six behind the leader. Rogers, Szoboszlai, Ndiaye, Calafiori and João Pedro made forty-five of it between them — five mid-price players rather than one lucky captain, which is the most repeatable week anybody had.
week.didnt: The Bench Boost, played in the first week of the season, returned six: two apiece from Kinsky, Diop and Groß, nothing from Konsa. His starting eleven scored fifty-eight, which is precisely Mr CR7’s total. The chip is not decoration on the lead — the chip is the lead.
week.next: Villa Park decides both ends of his squad in one fixture. Konsa, the £4.5m defender who returned nothing on his Bench Boost, is expected to make his Arsenal debut there against the club he left; Cash starts for the club he left it to, in a week where Villa have sold their centre-back, agreed to sell their goalkeeper, taken a free midfielder off Bayern and been asked publicly whether they are in crisis. One of those two is about to become a starter at a bench price and the other is about to face the champions. He does not need a transfer to profit from that — he needs the right eleven named tonight.

watchlist.name: Kayode
watchlist.note: Thirteen points from Brentford’s right-back at a hundred grand more than Cash, into a Leeds side that has scored in both its opening games. The cheaper way to replace a defender he cannot start.

watchlist.name: Ajer
watchlist.note: Eight points at exactly Cash’s price. Brentford have sold Pinnock to Coventry and bought a centre-back and a left-back in the same window, so the straight swap is less straight than it looked on Monday.

watchlist.name: Palmer
watchlist.note: Still the biggest collective miss of the season and it is getting louder, not quieter: thirteen points on the opening night, then a start, an assist and the best of Chelsea in the cup. Ownership 11.7% to 15.2% in a week while all five of them stood still.

watchlist.name: Ødegaard
watchlist.note: Eleven points at £6.6m. All five own an Arsenal defender, two of them own Tzolis at £6.5m, and nobody owns the Arsenal player who outscored both. This has now been written every day for a week, which makes it the page repeating itself rather than the room.

watchlist.name: Martinez
watchlist.note: A £5.0m goalkeeper who was dropped, wanted out, and now has an agreed £7.5m move to a club whose manager has spent a fortnight publicly hunting a goalkeeper. The player file still says Villa, so this is a Tuesday decision rather than a Friday one — but at that price it is the cheapest way to buy a settled first-choice job.

watchlist.name: Woltemade
watchlist.note: The trigger set two weeks ago was one start. He got the cup start, and the man he was behind has gone from a 50% knock to a foot injury with no return date. £6.0m, under 2% owned, in front of the kindest six-game run on the ticker.

watchlist.name: Trafford
watchlist.note: Two clean sheets from two at £5.0m and 4.2% owned. Cheap goalkeepers are bought for a floor and this one has produced a ceiling, which is usually the warning rather than the case — Brentford at Elland Road is the first honest test of it.

watchlist.name: Barry
watchlist.note: A hat-trick and an assist at Deepdale after a header on the opening day, in a side picked almost at full strength, at a club whose manager says publicly he still wants a number nine. Cup goals are a team sheet rather than a seat, and the team sheet was the part in doubt.

verdicts.name: Palmer
verdicts.why: Thirteen points and the penalties on the opening night, then a start and the assist for the second in the cup, with his manager framing the whole side around him.
verdicts.trigger: Two games spent wide rather than at ten, or the calf flag returning.

verdicts.name: João Pedro
verdicts.why: Eleven points, a rise to £7.6m and the number nine shirt — though Welbeck scoring on Thursday is the first evidence that the minutes are shared rather than owned.
verdicts.trigger: Two Chelsea games without a shot in the box, and 67.6% ownership becomes the risk rather than the floor.

verdicts.name: Rogers
verdicts.why: Tapped in on debut, got the full ninety, then started again in the cup and hit the bar — Chelsea keep picking him while Caicedo is out.
verdicts.trigger: A week wide or on the bench once Chelsea’s central midfield is whole again.

verdicts.name: Welbeck
verdicts.why: Headed the opener against Luton at 35 from a Gusto cross, his first since joining, and was singled out by his manager as the patient one who does what he does best.
verdicts.trigger: A league start. A £6.0m forward at 1% ownership who starts ahead of a 67%-owned one is a differential; one who comes on for him is not.

verdicts.name: Estêvão
verdicts.why: A thrilling display on the right in the cup and the shot that produced the second goal, at £6.5m and 1.2% ownership in an attack that is being rebuilt around Palmer.
verdicts.trigger: A league start on the right against Brighton. Cup form in an attacking side is a rehearsal until the weekend confirms it.

verdicts.name: James
verdicts.why: A £5.5m defender at 10% ownership who has now started in central midfield twice in three days despite a long injury history — no clean sheet points, no attacking returns, no zero.
verdicts.trigger: One start in the back line. Until then this is Hume’s problem in blue.

verdicts.name: Acheampong
verdicts.why: A £4.5m academy defender who started in Alonso’s back three at Fulham and played well, with clubs circling and loan talk before Tuesday.
verdicts.trigger: Selected again at home to Brighton on Sunday and this is the cheapest starting defender at a club with a kind opening run. Left out and he is gone.

verdicts.name: Sánchez
verdicts.why: The trigger was Chelsea getting through Tuesday without signing a goalkeeper. They did not: a £7.5m deal for Martinez is agreed and sources expect Sánchez to need moving on before the window shuts.
verdicts.trigger: Settled. Nothing left to watch here.

verdicts.name: Penders
verdicts.why: Made his debut in the cup and then watched Chelsea agree a deal for a 33-year-old World Cup winner over the top of him, with a loan now being discussed.
verdicts.trigger: The Martinez deal collapsing. Short of that, a 21-year-old third choice is not an FPL asset.

verdicts.name: Caicedo
verdicts.why: Missed the cup tie too, so Chelsea have now played three competitive games with a makeshift pivot and Reece James in midfield.
verdicts.trigger: Ninety minutes against Brighton. Until then every Chelsea midfielder’s minutes are being set by an absence.

verdicts.name: Enzo
verdicts.why: Left out of the cup tie entirely with City expected to bid within 48 hours, and his manager’s answers did nothing to suggest he will play for Chelsea again.
verdicts.trigger: The deadline passing with him at Chelsea and starting in central midfield. Reported at £120m and possibly rising, that is not the way to bet.

verdicts.name: Palestra
verdicts.why: Flagged at 75% again and still without a competitive minute for the club, while a 20-year-old on £1.0m less starts in the back three ahead of him.
verdicts.trigger: One competitive start. Until then this is a slot rather than a player.

verdicts.name: Lacroix
verdicts.why: Six points at £6.0m from a back line that conceded twice, and Chelsea have just agreed £40m for another centre-back with the window four days from shutting.
verdicts.trigger: A clean sheet against a Brighton side missing four forwards. If it does not come now, it is not coming.

verdicts.name: Martinez
verdicts.why: A £5.0m goalkeeper out of favour behind Suzuki has an agreed £7.5m move and a two-year deal at a club that identified a goalkeeper as its priority signing — the seat goes from gone to guaranteed in one afternoon.
verdicts.trigger: The move completing and the player file moving him to Chelsea. Buying an agreed deal before it is done is buying a rumour at a starter’s price.

verdicts.name: Suzuki
verdicts.why: The reason Villa’s previous number one was dropped and is now leaving, at £5.0m and 0.8% ownership.
verdicts.trigger: A clean sheet in the next three. Villa’s defence has lost Konsa, is being rebuilt in public and faces Arsenal first, so the seat is safe and the points are the question.

verdicts.name: Cash
verdicts.why: Minus one in a 4-0, and the week since has produced a sold centre-back, a goalkeeper with an agreed exit, a free signing from Bayern and a Football Weekly segment asking whether Villa are in crisis. Arsenal at Villa Park is next.
verdicts.trigger: Two clean sheets in three, or the window closing with the dressing room settled.

verdicts.name: Watkins
verdicts.why: A reported Saudi fee agreed and a replacement striker signed, four days from the deadline.
verdicts.trigger: The deadline passing with him at Villa and in the starting eleven.

verdicts.name: B.Fernandes
verdicts.why: PFA Player of the Year on Tuesday, and a team described as playing with zero cohesion and conviction at Hull on Saturday. The award is about last season.
verdicts.trigger: A blank at home to Ipswich with the same shot profile, and £12.0m stops being a price and starts being a hole.

verdicts.name: Mbeumo
verdicts.why: Two points, and the Hull post-mortem points at shot quality rather than at the two set plays — the slower problem, not the quicker one.
verdicts.trigger: United blanking at home to Ipswich, which makes the GW4 sale automatic.

verdicts.name: Shaw
verdicts.why: Thirty-one, PFA Player of the Year in the same week his side lost at a promoted club, and still the position United are reported to want to reinforce before Tuesday.
verdicts.trigger: A left-back arriving before the deadline, or one week out of the side. Either ends a £4.5m pick whose entire case is that he never misses.

verdicts.name: Lammens
verdicts.why: Cheap is not the same as safe behind a defence that lost at Hull to two headers, and there is a £5.0m goalkeeper with two clean sheets from two on the same shelf.
verdicts.trigger: Two clean sheets in the next three, or enough save points to make the floor worth it.

verdicts.name: Maguire
verdicts.why: One point, and he is the defender in the middle of the set plays United conceded — though with De Ligt out there is currently nobody to take the shirt.
verdicts.trigger: Losing his place when United’s other centre-backs are fit.

verdicts.name: Calafiori
verdicts.why: Nine points, a rise to £5.6m, owned by four of the five and by 41.6% of the game — still the closest thing to a free lunch on the list.
verdicts.trigger: A recurrence of the knee trouble that has followed him around, or the Champions League draw against Real Madrid producing genuine rotation.

verdicts.name: Ødegaard
verdicts.why: Eleven points at £6.6m and a week later still nobody in the room owns him, which has stopped being an oversight and become a choice.
verdicts.trigger: A repeat of last season’s injury record, or Arsenal’s returns concentrating in Saka and Gyökeres instead.

verdicts.name: Saka
verdicts.why: Nine points and Arsenal’s penalties at £9.5m, with barely 10% of the game on him.
verdicts.trigger: The recurring hamstring, or rotation once Real Madrid appear on the calendar.

verdicts.name: Havertz
verdicts.why: Six points at £7.5m and 7.3% ownership, in a forward line that has not settled around Gyökeres and whose club is still chasing another striker.
verdicts.trigger: Arsenal signing a forward before Tuesday, or two weeks as a substitute.

verdicts.name: Mosquera
verdicts.why: Six points deputising while both Saliba and Timber are out with no return date — the points are real and the seat is borrowed, and the £55m man behind him is now expected to play.
verdicts.trigger: Konsa starting at Villa Park. That is this pick ending, not threatening to.

verdicts.name: Konsa
verdicts.why: A £4.5m defender at 11% ownership expected to make his Arsenal debut at Villa Park against the club he spent seven seasons at, in a defence missing both first-choice centre-backs.
verdicts.trigger: Named in the eleven and this is the cheapest starting defender at the champions. Left out again and the price is the only thing recommending him.

verdicts.name: White
verdicts.why: Eleven points, the highest of any Arsenal defender, at £5.5m and 6.5% ownership — and the reason is the same injury list that put Mosquera in the side.
verdicts.trigger: Timber’s groin clearing, which returns him to a rotation option at a starter’s price.

verdicts.name: Tzolis
verdicts.why: Six points and a debut that got noticed; 26% of the game is on him now and the price has not moved.
verdicts.trigger: Saka and Rice fully fit squeezing the minutes.

verdicts.name: Szoboszlai
verdicts.why: Central midfield at Newcastle and on Liverpool’s penalties at £7.0m, owned by three of the five — but Iraola has spent the week saying the midfield problem is on the training ground, and it is the midfield he is in.
verdicts.trigger: Mac Allister starting in the pivot, or a shift back to right-back. Either halves the appeal.

verdicts.name: Gravenberch
verdicts.why: Lost the ball for both Newcastle goals, and Forest — whose Gibbs-White has feasted in exactly that space at Anfield before — arrive on Saturday with Delap registered in time to play.
verdicts.trigger: A clean sheet against Forest, or one week out of the pivot. Iraola says it is not personnel; Saturday is where that gets tested.

verdicts.name: Gakpo
verdicts.why: The trigger was the window shutting with no wide forward arriving. Instead Liverpool have agreed £120m for Barcola, which is not a fee you pay for a substitute.
verdicts.trigger: Settled by the transfer rather than by a scoreline. Revisit only if the Barcola deal collapses.

verdicts.name: Kerkez
verdicts.why: Ninety minutes at left-back at Newcastle and Liverpool’s window money has gone to a £120m winger rather than to a full-back.
verdicts.trigger: One week on the bench, or Liverpool moving to a back three, and £5.5m stops making sense.

verdicts.name: Haaland
verdicts.why: Two points, ninety minutes, the penalties and the armband from three of the five — a blank that separated nobody, and City have spent the window selling the forwards behind him rather than buying one.
verdicts.trigger: A serious injury, or three straight weeks of City creating through the wide players and past him.

verdicts.name: Gvardiol
verdicts.why: Started at left-back and returned nine — and with Guéhi being used in central midfield, he is increasingly the only City defender you can name in advance.
verdicts.trigger: O’Reilly reclaiming the left side once Doku is back on 5 September.

verdicts.name: Guéhi
verdicts.why: Ten points, but they came from a corner headed in while he was playing the blocker role in central midfield — and Maresca may use him there again at Palace tonight. A defender who is not in the defence does not get clean sheet points.
verdicts.trigger: Two games in the back line. £6.0m for a centre-back playing midfield is the wrong shape of bet however the first one landed.

verdicts.name: Cherki
verdicts.why: Eight points from the bench, with Marmoush now gone to Spurs and an £85m 18-year-old arriving who his manager expects to start on the bench.
verdicts.trigger: A start. The trigger set three weeks ago has not changed and still has not been met.

verdicts.name: Semenyo
verdicts.why: Two points at £8.5m from a starting City wide role, at 24.4% ownership — the most owned player in the game who has given nobody a reason.
verdicts.trigger: Two more blanks with Cherki getting the minutes instead, and this is a sack.

verdicts.name: Marmoush
verdicts.why: The loan to Spurs is done, which turns a fourth-choice City forward into a possible starter for a side whose manager says it is not a team yet — but the player file still has him at City and priced as one.
verdicts.trigger: A start at Spurs. The move is no longer the question; the shirt is.

verdicts.name: M.Sangaré
verdicts.why: Fourteen on debut and a rise to £5.6m, but the case is the defensive-contribution rate rather than the two assists, and Brentford have kept buying midfielders all window.
verdicts.trigger: Two more weeks over the threshold and he is the cheap midfielder of the season. One is a debut.

verdicts.name: Ajer
verdicts.why: Eight points at £4.5m in a side whose press left Spurs without a shot on target until 3-0 down — but Brentford have sold Pinnock and bought both a centre-back and a left-back this window.
verdicts.trigger: One rotation, or Schuster starting a league game. A £4.5m centre-back at a club buying defenders is a seat on loan.

verdicts.name: Kayode
verdicts.why: Thirteen points and a rise to £4.6m from Brentford’s right-back, and the £40m left-back arriving plays on the other side.
verdicts.trigger: A week out of the side, or the returns turning out to have been one afternoon of set pieces.

verdicts.name: Thiago
verdicts.why: Missed from the spot after converting ten of his previous eleven, blanked in a 3-0 win, and now meets a Leeds goalkeeper with two clean sheets from two.
verdicts.trigger: Losing the penalties to anyone, and £8.0m is a sack the same day.

verdicts.name: Calvert-Lewin
verdicts.why: Leeds play through him and he started; a one-point opener is a dull floor, which is what four of the five bought him for.
verdicts.trigger: Losing the penalties, or Leeds signing the £30m winger they are chasing and changing the shape around him.

verdicts.name: Trafford
verdicts.why: Two clean sheets from two opening games at £5.0m and 4.2% ownership, in the season’s cheapest goalkeeper bracket where everybody else is buying a floor.
verdicts.trigger: Brentford at Elland Road. A third clean sheet against a side that scored three at Spurs and this is the goalkeeper of the first quarter.

verdicts.name: Ndiaye
verdicts.why: Nine points on Everton’s penalties at £6.0m, he kept his place in a near-full-strength cup eleven, and his manager has made public that he is desperate to keep him.
verdicts.trigger: A bid landing before Tuesday, or the penalty duty moving.

verdicts.name: Dewsbury-Hall
verdicts.why: Eleven points and the opener in a 2-0, then the pass for the first and the drive that made the second at Deepdale — Everton’s chances go through him at £6.5m and 4.5% ownership.
verdicts.trigger: A second blank in three with Everton conceding, and he goes back to being a hedge.

verdicts.name: Barry
verdicts.why: A hat-trick and an assist in the cup after a header on the opening day, at £5.5m and 3% ownership, with his manager still saying publicly that the squad needs a forward.
verdicts.trigger: A league goal, or Everton signing the number nine Moyes keeps asking for. One of those makes him, one ends him.

verdicts.name: Tarkowski
verdicts.why: A £6.0m centre-back travelling to a side that conceded eighteen set-piece goals last season and hired its first set-piece coach because of it.
verdicts.trigger: A goal or a clean sheet at Bournemouth. Everton away has been a good bet for two seasons; this is the fixture to price it on.

verdicts.name: Woltemade
verdicts.why: The cup start came, and the striker ahead of him has gone from a 50% knock to a foot injury with no return date. £6.0m, on penalties, 1.6% owned, in front of the best six-game run on the ticker.
verdicts.trigger: Spurs away without a league start. That would mean the seat was never his and the fixtures were never the point.

verdicts.name: Osula
verdicts.why: A 50% knock on Wednesday is a foot injury with no return date today, four days from the deadline.
verdicts.trigger: A return date. The Newcastle striker slot is the other one now.

verdicts.name: Kinsky
verdicts.why: Owned by three of the five, behind a defence assembled from World Cup finalists who missed most of pre-season — Van de Ven, Porro, Udogie and Bentancur are all still catching up after a 26-hour tour their manager did not want.
verdicts.trigger: Reassess at GW7 — window shut, players settled, fixtures softer. Until then this is a bench goalkeeper.

verdicts.name: Tonali
verdicts.why: A £92.5m signing his manager did not think fit enough to finish the opener, publicly confirmed to start against his old club on Saturday after a week of targeted conditioning work.
verdicts.trigger: Ninety minutes against Newcastle. A £5.5m midfielder who runs a Premier League side is worth owning; one who is being managed back to fitness is not.

verdicts.name: Hume
verdicts.why: Sunderland pushed him forward into a right-wing role — good for assists, bad for the clean sheets he was bought for — and Mukiele’s fitness is what would put him back.
verdicts.trigger: A second week out of the back line. A £4.5m defender who does not defend is priced wrong for the position.

verdicts.name: E.Le Fée
verdicts.why: Plenty of the ball and Sunderland going through him, but no shots and no chances created at £6.0m, in a side being publicly written off as relegation candidates.
verdicts.trigger: A return in the next two, or the money goes to a midfielder who takes shots.

verdicts.name: Igor Jesus
verdicts.why: Forest’s club-record striker is signed, registered and available to play at Anfield on Saturday.
verdicts.trigger: Keeping the shirt for two starts with the new man fit. Settled otherwise.

verdicts.name: De Cuyper
verdicts.why: Seventeen points at £4.6m, and Brighton go to Stamford Bridge without Mitoma, Minteh and Tzimas and with two more flagged — the attacking returns were the case and the attack is the injured part.
verdicts.trigger: A second attacking return with that forward line unavailable, and this is a buy rather than an argument.

verdicts.name: Verbruggen
verdicts.why: A clean sheet in a 4-0 at £4.5m, which is the entire job description of this pick — but the next one is at Chelsea.
verdicts.trigger: Steele getting a cup start that turns into a league one.

signals.text: Chelsea have agreed a £7.5m deal to sign Emiliano Martinez from Aston Villa, with Alonso having identified a goalkeeper as the priority after Sánchez struggled against Fulham. Sources believe Sánchez is unlikely to accept losing his spot as No 1 and may need to be moved on before the window shuts on Tuesday night.
signals.action: the trigger written on Monday was Chelsea getting through Tuesday without signing a goalkeeper. They did not. The sack is settled and the Chelsea goalkeeper slot now belongs to somebody else

signals.text: Out of favour at Villa after the arrival of Zion Suzuki, and due to sign a two-year contract with the option of a further year at Chelsea. He turns 34 next week.
signals.action: a £5.0m goalkeeper going from dropped to first choice at a club with a soft opening run is the cheapest job upgrade in the game — but the deal is agreed rather than done, and the player file still says Villa. This is a Tuesday buy

signals.text: Left out of the Carabao Cup tie against Luton with City poised to bid within 48 hours. Chelsea insist there has been no communication from City and that he will be sold only on their terms, with the price possibly rising above the £120m City missed an unofficial deadline to pay.
signals.action: a vice-captain omitted from a home cup tie to protect the team from the noise has played his last game for the club. There is nothing left to hold at £7.0m

signals.text: Headed Chelsea in front against Luton from a Gusto cross for his first goal since joining from Brighton. Alonso: "Danny was the patient player. He did what he does best: score and to be in the right place."
signals.action: the £6.0m forward at 1% ownership is competition for the £7.6m one at 67.6%. That does not make him a buy; it makes João Pedro slightly less of a lock than the ownership implies

signals.text: Started in central midfield for the second time in three days, despite his injury problems, with Caicedo still unavailable.
signals.action: a £5.5m defender at 10% ownership who is being used as a midfielder scores like neither. Nobody in this room owns him and nobody should until Caicedo is back

signals.text: The 20-year-old academy graduate started in Alonso’s back three against Fulham and played well. Several clubs are interested and there is talk of a loan before the window shuts; being selected again on Sunday against Brighton would strengthen his position at the club.
signals.action: a £4.5m defender in a starting back three is the cheapest way into Chelsea’s opening run. Sunday’s team sheet is the whole of the case, and it comes after the deadline

signals.text: Liverpool have agreed a £120m deal for Paris St-Germain’s Bradley Barcola after breakthrough talks, having had two bids for Minteh rejected and seen Sarr go down with a groin injury.
signals.action: the trigger was the window shutting with nobody arriving. Somebody arrived, at £120m, in his position. Twelve points on the opening weekend was the top of this, not the start of it

signals.text: A centre-back by trade, he was a surprise selection in the blocker role next to Elliot Anderson against Bournemouth, scored the 84th-minute equaliser from a corner, and may be used there again at Crystal Palace with the £85m Bouaddi expected to start on the bench.
signals.action: ten points from a defender who was not in the defence. He is 19.3% owned and the ownership is buying a clean sheet he is not positioned to keep

signals.text: Expected to be able to make his Arsenal debut at Villa Park against the club he spent seven seasons at, having joined from them this summer.
signals.action: the trigger on a £4.5m defender at 11% ownership was one start, and one of the five has him sitting on a bench. If he is named, that is the cheapest starting defender at the champions

signals.text: Left out of the Charlton cup tie along with Senesi for an intense training session instead. De Zerbi: "Sandro has to work to feel better in terms of physical condition, but on Saturday he will play in the first XI." He faces Newcastle, who sold him for £92.5m in July.
signals.action: a confirmed start is worth more than most of what gets called team news. £5.5m for the midfielder a side is built around, if the conditioning has taken

signals.text: Now carrying a foot injury with no return date, having been listed at 50% with a knock two days ago when Woltemade started the cup tie in his place.

signals.text: Moyes is described as desperate to hang on to him as the window closes, with Everton having spent the summer on midfield and squad depth rather than on forwards.
signals.action: two of the five own him at £6.0m and the risk was always a bid rather than the football. Four days to go

doctrine.text: Rank insurance is a real cost — price the drift on every call.
New-manager minutes are unknowable until three XIs.
Champions' template assets are default-own; passing needs a priced case.
Opening weekend prices nothing. A promoted side beating a giant is one result until the same shape holds twice — sell on a pattern, never on a scoreline.
A cheap-defender haul is a match, not a seat. Before buying points that already happened, check the player is still fit and still first choice.

Grade a chip against its own median week — and then check the table before saying it did not matter. Six points from a Bench Boost is a chip spent rather than used; it is also, exactly, the six points between first of the five and second.

Buy the line-up, not the scoreboard. Three of the weekend’s best mid-price returns came from players who started on a bench or out of position, and two of the room’s bench slots are held by players who have not been in a matchday eleven.

A player the whole room passed on is a bigger exposure than a player the whole room owns. All five owned Haaland and João Pedro; none owned Palmer, who outscored both. Check the consensus blind spot before checking the consensus pick.
An open window is a team-sheet risk, not a shopping opportunity. Buy after the window shuts, not into it.

A cup tie is a team sheet, not a fixture. The goals are worth nothing and the selection is worth everything — which is why a 35-year-old’s header, a flagged striker’s replacement and a vice-captain’s absence were the three things worth reading on Thursday night.

Write triggers a transfer can settle, not only ones that need ninety minutes. Two calls were resolved this week without a ball being kicked: the Chelsea goalkeeper, because Chelsea signed one, and the Liverpool winger, because Liverpool bought over him. A trigger that only a scoreline can fire will sit open through the weeks that actually decide the player.

roast.text: Mr CR7 left twelve points on his bench, nine of them Gvardiol, playing at the Etihad. Somewhere in that team sheet is a man who looked at a City defender at home and decided it was too risky.

plan.outlook: Deadline night, and the table has not moved since Monday: Le Professeur 64 and second of eleven, Mr CR7 58, Xabi 50, Sir Fergie 49, The Special One 48, with Gunners.exe out in front on 70. Sixteen points cover the five, which is still one bench ordering. What has moved is everything the money was arguing about a week ago, and most of it settled against a wait-and-see. Chelsea have agreed £7.5m for a goalkeeper and £40m for a centre-back, and left their vice-captain out of a home cup tie. Liverpool have agreed £120m for a winger, which ends the Gakpo case rather than opening it. Villa have sold a centre-back, agreed to sell a goalkeeper and taken a free midfielder off Bayern, and host Arsenal. Newcastle’s first-choice striker has gone from a knock to no return date. Four days of noise resolved into four days of signings, which is exactly what D9 said would happen and exactly why nothing was bought into it. The consequence tonight is that only two decisions are actually live: the armband, which is a choice between a striker who blanked and a midfielder whose team played without cohesion at Hull, and whether anybody in this room finally buys the Arsenal midfielder or the Chelsea one. Everything else is a Tuesday decision wearing a Friday costume. Three of the five have a free transfer and no obligation to spend it, and the honest recommendation for the sixth run running is that they should not.

chips.note: First-half chips die at the GW19 deadline (2 Jan). A good week used beats a perfect week hoarded — but the worst week to spend a chip is one in which the team sheets are being written by a transfer window, and that has been true of every week so far. It stops being true on Wednesday. The first real chip conversation is GW6–8, post-break, with three settled line-ups behind it.

log.call: Day-0 squad: Haaland (C) vs BOU; bets on Palmer, Kerkez, Hume; passed on Bruno Fernandes at £12.0m with Mbeumo/Shaw/Lammens carrying the Man Utd run.

Held again with GW1 unfinished: no transfer, the free one banked to Friday, all three United men kept into Ipswich at home. Haaland (C) at Selhurst Park, B.Fernandes vice, 3-4-3 unchanged. Declined the Hull £4.0m defenders after their haul.

No move with Gameweek 1 one fixture from finished. Declined all three of the weekend's obvious buys — the Hull £4.0m defenders (all flagged at 75%), Sangaré's fourteen on debut, and Cherki's eight off the bench — on the grounds that a doubt or a substitute is not a seat. Graded Le Professeur's Gameweek 1 Bench Boost as spent rather than used at six points, while conceding he leads the five without it.

Settled Gameweek 1 at fifty points and fifth of eleven. Upgraded Palmer to nailed after thirteen on the opening night and named him, with Ødegaard, as the room's shape rather than its luck — neither is owned by any of the five. Sacked Palestra and Aït-Nouri as slots rather than players after both missed their clubs' matchday elevens, and sacked Cash and Watkins on Villa's week rather than on Villa's fixture. Recommended no transfer before Friday: every obvious buy is either one game old, flagged, or in the middle of a transfer.

No transfer recommended for the third run running, two days before the deadline and six before the window shuts — on the explicit grounds that an open window is a team-sheet risk rather than a shopping opportunity (D9). Downgraded Shaw on the reporting that United expect another left-back before Tuesday. Flipped the Gakpo case: the risk is no longer that Liverpool sell him but that they buy over him, with two bids rejected for one winger and two more targets live. Sacked Villa's goalkeeper as a slot, and Forest's incumbent striker on a £50m arrival. Corrected two errors of our own from Monday: The Special One's dead men were on his bench, not in his eleven, and Le Professeur's six-point Bench Boost is not a footnote to his lead, it is the whole of it.

Deadline eve, and no transfer recommended for the fifth run running — Friday’s deadline falls four days before the window shuts, so nothing bought now is bought with the team sheet known. Upgraded Woltemade on Osula’s knock and a cup start, and opened Barry at £5.5m on a hat-trick graded as a team sheet rather than a scoreline. Held Palestra at sack after Alonso said Chelsea "need to check a little bit more" ahead of a second missed fixture, and added the goalkeeper question alongside it. Cooled De Cuyper on Brighton’s injury list rather than on his seventeen points, and warned on Ajer as Brentford bought a fifth player and sold a centre-back. Sacked Baleba, Osula and Grealish as slots rather than players. Minted D10: a cup tie is a team sheet, not a fixture.

Deadline day. No transfer recommended for the sixth run running, on the grounds that the deadline falls four days before the window shuts and every squad in the room already has fifteen fit players. Settled two calls by transfer rather than by result: sacked Sánchez outright once Chelsea agreed £7.5m for Martinez, the exact trigger written on Monday, and killed the Gakpo case once Liverpool agreed £120m for Barcola — the trigger there was the window shutting with nobody arriving, and somebody arrived. Opened Martinez at £5.0m as a Tuesday buy rather than a Friday one, with Suzuki alongside him. Upgraded Woltemade to solid as Osula went from a 50% knock to no return date, and Konsa on the reporting that he starts at Villa Park. Downgraded Penders to sack behind the new goalkeeper. Cooled Guéhi on the grounds that his ten points came from central midfield, where a defender keeps no clean sheets. Opened Estêvão, James, Acheampong, Trafford, Tarkowski and Tonali. Minted D11: write triggers a transfer can settle, not only ones that need ninety minutes.
